source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's SAT1 campus in San Antonio publishes 9 MW of IT capacity across 110,000 square feet, making it a mid-sized Texas data center whose AI relevance depends entirely on how much power it can draw.

The 9 MW is the only power figure CyrusOne discloses. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, that load implies roughly 225 racks, but this is arithmetic on an assumption rather than a published specification. The operator publishes no rack count, no GPU count, and no tenant roster, so any accelerator estimate is a modeling choice.

The certification list, PCI DSS, HIPAA, ISO 27001, FISMA, SSAE 16 Type II, and TIA-942, qualifies the campus for regulated workloads including payment card data, protected health information, and federal systems. Certifications describe what the facility is permitted to handle, not who occupies it.

Texas holds 137 mapped facilities, of which only 19 publish a megawatt figure, totaling 475.41 MW. SAT1 ranks 14th in the state by published megawatts, but that rank sits within a small disclosed subset rather than the state's full buildout. Most Texas facilities disclose nothing, so the published record understates the state's actual capacity.
